name: Albany
objection: As a city it may be a destination rather than a spot; that is the proposer's call, not a reason to drop it.

name: Denmark
objection: Its headline draws (Greens Pool, Elephant Rocks) are separate candidates, so the town must not become a wrapper for them; it stays only for its own base role and inlet setting.

name: Walpole
objection: Its draws (Tree Top Walk, Nornalup Inlet, Coalmine Beach) are separate candidates, so the town risks being a wrapper; the proposer should place it as a base/destination name rather than a spot beside its own attractions.

name: Mount Barker
objection: No Wikivoyage article of its own and the town has little to see itself; if the Porongurup/Stirling Range spots carry the visit, it may only be a gateway at a low rank.

name: Bremer Bay
objection: The headline (Bremer Canyon orcas) is an offshore cruise and seasonal (Jan-Apr); the town's own sights are beaches named in passing. The board page was read only through search results (the site blocks scripts).

name: Kojonup
objection: Against: its one real draw, The Kodja Place, is a separate candidate, so the town would be a wrapper beside its own attraction (COVERAGE 'A town is a spot only when the town itself is a draw'); a service stop on Albany Highway rather than a base.

name: Katanning
objection: A wheatbelt-edge service town most travellers pass through; the attractions are modest and some (saleyard auctions) are weekly.

name: Katanning All Ages Playground
objection: Against: it is a playground, close to the 'ordinary suburban park' negative benchmark; the shire's own page is not independent of the board; better as a reason in Katanning's bio than its own spot.

name: Albany Convict Gaol
objection: Small volunteer-run museum; overlaps in theme with the Museum of the Great Southern and Patrick Taylor Cottage nearby.

name: Albany Wind Farm
objection: It is infrastructure; the visit is a boardwalk and lookout of 30-60 minutes.

name: Brig Amity Replica
objection: Against: Visit Albany says 'the Amity is part of the Museum of the Great Southern site on Residency Road', so it may be part of a larger spot (rule 3); volunteer-staffed with variable hours. Either keep it as its own spot or fold it into the Museum of the Great Southern's bio.

name: Patrick Taylor Cottage
objection: Small volunteer-run house museum, a 30-45 minute visit with limited hours.

name: Princess Royal Fortress
objection: Visitors and the board name it the National ANZAC Centre; the proposer should consider that name (or both) so search finds it.

name: Albany Historic Whaling Station
objection: None of substance; note the Wikipedia title is 'Cheynes Beach Whaling Station', which is a near-name of the separate Cheynes Beach (a different place 60 km east).

name: Dog Rock
objection: A 5-10 minute look beside a road near supermarkets; only one counted source.

name: Old Post Office, Albany
objection: Wikivoyage also says it now houses restaurants and a weaver; whether the museum is still open is unconfirmed, and with one source and a short visit it is marginal (a building on the Stirling Terrace heritage walk rather than a destination in itself).

name: Mount Clarence
objection: A town hill some would call a local reserve; it survives on the memorial and the views, which is why it absorbs the memorial candidate.

name: Mount Melville
objection: Against: no counted source could be opened (Visit Albany's walks and parks pages do not name it), reviewers report the upper stairs closed and trees blocking views; Mount Clarence and Mount Adelaide are Albany's promoted lookouts.

name: Quaranup Point Possession Trail
objection: Against: only one counted source, short, and not among Visit Albany's 10 Great Walks; no coordinates yet.

name: Bibbulmun Track
objection: It runs 963 km across three WA regions (Perth Hills to Albany); it must be one spot across the whole run, not one per region, and its pin and region need coordinating with the Perth and South West judges.

name: Munda Biddi Trail
objection: Like the Bibbulmun it spans several regions, so one spot overall; it is a cycling route used mostly by dedicated riders, a narrower draw than the walking track.

name: Middleton Beach
objection: A town beach; its name in Noongar (Binalup) may be the form to use.

name: Frenchman Bay
objection: A sheltered local swimming bay; less of a draw than Misery Beach nearby.

name: Goode Beach
objection: Against: no counted source names Goode Beach itself as a place to go (Visit Albany's beaches page omits it); it is a residential suburb beach.

name: Muttonbird Island
objection: Against: the candidate as named is the island, a reserve with no visitor use; the beach is 4WD-dependent for much of its length and mainly a local surf/fishing spot.

name: Betty's Beach
objection: Against: no counted visitor source beyond a motoring-club list; a fishing and camping beach used by professional fishermen in autumn; lean reject.

name: Nanarup Beach
objection: Mostly a local surf and 4WD beach; the lagoon is a 15-minute walk.

name: Cheynes Beach
objection: Rough water, not for swimming; 50 minutes east of Albany and mostly a fishing/4WD beach.

name: Misery Beach
objection: None strong; it is inside Torndirrup NP, so the proposer should make sure the park and the beach are not duplicates.

name: The Gap
objection: It lies inside Torndirrup National Park, which is also kept; the park needs a different visitor point and photo from this spot. (The DBCA site URL in the candidate is a 404; the park page and board listing carry it.)

name: Blowholes
objection: Spectacular only with a big swell; otherwise a short coastal walk.

name: Salmon Holes
objection: Dangerous water (Visit Albany warns of rips); visitors mostly stop at the lookout.

name: Jimmy Newells
objection: A short stop (15-20 minutes); could be folded into Torndirrup's text.

name: Bald Head Walk Trail
objection: Within Torndirrup NP; ensure it is not duplicated with a 'Bald Head' or 'Flinders Peninsula' entry.

name: Stony Hill Heritage Trail
objection: A 20-30 minute loop within Torndirrup NP.

name: Torndirrup National Park
objection: Its best-known feature is a separate spot; the park must take another visitor point (Blowholes or Salmon Holes) so it is not a near-duplicate of The Gap.

name: HMAS Perth Wreck
objection: Only certified divers can visit (via dive shops), so most visitors cannot do anything there; could be held to review if the owner wants land-reachable spots only.

name: Gull Rock National Park
objection: A small park popular mainly with locals; its single named site is Ledge Beach.

name: Two Peoples Bay Nature Reserve
objection: Little Beach, its headline, is a separate spot; the reserve must not duplicate it (pin it at the visitor centre).

name: Little Beach
objection: Two Peoples Bay Nature Reserve may also be a candidate; if both are kept they need distinct points (Little Beach is the reserve's best-known stop).

name: West Cape Howe National Park
objection: Most of the park needs a 4WD; the 2WD visit is Shelley Beach and its lookout (keep the pins apart).

name: Shelley Beach
objection: Not safe for swimming; overlaps the park entry, so the park and the beach need different pins.

name: Torbay Head
objection: Against: reached only by 4WD or a long sandy walk, mostly seen from Shelley Beach; likely folded into West Cape Howe National Park.

name: Waterfall Beach
objection: Against: Visit Albany treats it as an extension of a Little Beach visit (part of a larger spot), no counted page of its own. Note: DBCA's 'Waterfall Beach' page is a different place in William Bay NP near Denmark, which the enumeration may have missed and should be judged on its own.

name: Fitzgerald River National Park
objection: Remote with gravel access from Bremer Bay and Hopetoun; the whole park sits in this region per the boundary brief.

name: Point Ann
objection: Its headline is seasonal; outside June-October it is a beach and heritage walk in Fitzgerald River NP.

name: Whalebone Beach
objection: Remote: reached only by 4WD when the track is open, otherwise on foot via the Hakea Trail; both counted sources are DBCA (not independent), and few visitors get there.

name: West Mount Barren
objection: None strong; overlaps the Barren Range entry, which should not also be kept.

name: Quoin Head
objection: Remote, 4WD access; both counted sources are DBCA.

name: St Mary Inlet
objection: No formal paths; the visit is mainly camping or a look on the way to Point Ann.

name: Hamersley Inlet
objection: One agency page plus a Wikivoyage camping line; a quiet place mostly for campers.

name: Hakea Trail
objection: No length, trailhead or trail page found; a gallery caption is a thin source.

name: Mount Hassell
objection: One counted source, and a lesser peak beside Toolbrunup; an owner could treat it as marginal.

name: Dillon Bay
objection: No tourism board, DBCA or guidebook names it; ExplorOz and BeachSafe are not counted sources.

name: Denmark Historical Museum
objection: Single source, short visit, local interest only.

name: William Bay National Park
objection: Greens Pool and Elephant Rocks are separate spots and are why most visit; the park keeps only a different visitor point (Madfish Bay or Waterfall Beach) and photo. DBCA notes some path closures during works, but the park stays open.

name: Greens Pool
objection: None of substance.

name: Elephant Rocks
objection: It is a 10-minute walk from Greens Pool and many visit both in one stop, so it could be argued as part of Greens Pool; DBCA and the board list it as its own site, so it stays separate.

name: Ocean Beach
objection: Strong rips near the inlet; a beach mainly for surfers in cool water.

name: Walpole-Nornalup National Park
objection: Most of its draws are separate candidates (Valley of the Giants, Giant Tingle Tree, Circular Pool, Coalmine Beach); the park as a spot must take its own visitor point, not one of theirs.

name: Valley of the Giants Tree Top Walk
objection: None; the Ancient Empire boardwalk at the same site is part of it, not a second spot.

name: Giant Tingle Tree
objection: Shares Hilltop Road with Hilltop Lookout; may be seen as part of one Hilltop drive.

name: Hilltop Lookout
objection: A ten-minute look on the way to the Giant Tingle Tree.

name: Circular Pool
objection: Short visit, mainly a picnic spot.

name: Coalmine Beach
objection: An inlet beach mainly used by those staying at the adjacent holiday park.

name: Irwin Inlet
objection: Locals' fishing spot; overlaps Peaceful Bay.

name: Mount Clare
objection: Candidate flagged as a disambiguation: confirm it is the Walpole Wilderness Mount Clare (not Albany's Mount Clarence) before pinning.

name: Conspicuous Beach
objection: None strong; name choice (Cliff vs Beach) to settle with the proposer.

name: Porongurup National Park
objection: Castle Rock and the Granite Skywalk are a separate spot and its headline; the park needs another visitor point (Tree in the Rock picnic area) to stay distinct.

name: Granite Skywalk
objection: Two names for one walk and rock; must not ship as two spots.

name: Castle Rock
objection: The draw is the Granite Skywalk; the proposer may name the spot 'Castle Rock Granite Skywalk' so visitors recognise it.

name: Devils Slide
objection: Shares a trailhead area with the Tree in the Rock circuit; secondary to the Granite Skywalk.

name: Stirling Range National Park
objection: Bluff Knoll is a separate spot; the park needs a different point (Stirling Range Drive or Mount Trio/Toolbrunup).

name: Bluff Knoll
objection: None of substance.

name: Mount Trio
objection: Lesser-known than Bluff Knoll and Toolbrunup; both sources are DBCA.

name: Toolbrunup Peak
objection: Both sources are DBCA; a fit-walkers' summit.

name: Stirling Range Scenic Drive
objection: Drives are routes, not places; it duplicates the park.

name: Cape Riche
objection: A campground listing is not a visitor 'See' entry; mostly anglers and campers.

name: Oyster Harbour
objection: Its visitor point is Emu Point.

name: Valley of the Giants
objection: Two board listings for the same site; must not ship twice.

name: The Kodja Place
objection: One counted source; a small-town centre visitors mostly reach passing through on the Albany Highway.

name: Museum of the Great Southern
objection: Candidate coordinates are the WA Museum in Perth (redirect); the pin must be resolved at Residency Road, Albany. Wikivoyage lists the Residency Museum and the Brig Amity separately, a duplication risk.

name: Denmark Animal Farm and Pentland Alpaca Stud
objection: A small commercial farm attraction with a shop.

name: East Mount Barren
objection: One counted source; a hard short climb.

name: Lights Beach
objection: Rule 3 risk: close to Greens Pool and Elephant Rocks; the DBCA page sits under Greens Pool.

name: Emu Point
objection: Partly a suburb and holiday-park area; it is the visitor point of Oyster Harbour, so the two must not both ship.

name: Peaceful Bay
objection: One counted source; a holiday-shack village.

name: Wilson Inlet
objection: A 20 km water body has no single visitor point; overlaps Ocean Beach.

name: Yongernow Australian Malleefowl Centre
objection: Small volunteer-run centre in a tiny wheatbelt town; Lonely Planet itself says to check opening hours (closed Sun-Mon and public holidays), and visitors mostly stop in passing between the Stirling Range and Esperance/Ravensthorpe; only if nearby anyway on the friend test.
